title: Singing Domino Shine in Cabin in the Sky
summary: He sings his rewritten Shine lyrics and describes the strut up the stairs to Duke Ellington's band.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: What were you singing in 'Cabin in the Sky?'

sang to you.
"What is there about me that
Makes me feel well dressed
The same old clothes, shoes and hat
The same old things rearranged,
And it's very plain to see
Just how it happened to be.
I put some polish on my sky piece
I made a shoestring into a tie
I cut the corners off the end of my coat
So they wouldn't fly
I got my shirt from a silver lining
I made my cane from an old oak tree
And that is just the reason why
The folks all nicknamed me.
Just because -- my hair is curly
And because -- my teeth are pearly
And just because I always wear a smile
Suits to dress up in the latest style
Gee, I'm glad I'm living
I take troubles all with a smile
Because my color's shady
Wee bit different maybe
That's why they call me
That's why they call me Domino Shine"
So ended that paragraph.

So I did a strut to that,
you know. Duke Ellington's band was playing
and I was going to strut to that and I strut
up the stairs and I turned before the mirror
and everything -- see, I'm going up to get
Rochester who's upstairs and I'm going up to
the gambling room to get Rochester on on

out. So I go upstairs but they don't do nothin' after that, they cut.

I go upstairs to get Rochester, because he's up in the gambling room, I'm going to get him to even up the score for taking out Lena Horne. So we cut from that, that ended that scene. I finished the song, naturally, going upstairs to the room. When I say, "That's why they call me -- that's why they call me Shine." When I do that, I want to change that lyric Shine into Domino, but I didn't get to change it, it takes too much to do it, so they wouldn't change it. I hadn't thought of it before I got to the end of it. So I go upstairs and that's the end of that play, my part in the picture. But later on I get to shoot Rochester and Lena Horne, later on in the picture, in the play, rather in the picture, same thing.
